sources.title: Guido Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, full lecture notes
sources.locator: Full 119-page PDF fetched; inspected the complete relevant passages: Chapter 2 compact-operator spectral theorem and projections, PDF pp. 8–13; Chapter 3 compact singular systems and power notation, pp. 21–29; Chapter 4 Theorem 4.7, pp. 34–35; Chapter 5 qualification and discrepancy theorem, pp. 46–52; Chapter 6 Tikhonov source rates and saturation, pp. 55–58. Tikhonov minimizer context also inspected at Theorem 6.5, pp. 61–63.
sources.independent_treatment: Independent full graduate lecture-note treatment; counted as one of two independent A-page treatments.

contents.name: 2.1 inner products and weak convergence
contents.result: The Hilbert-space and induced-norm discussion supplies context; the complete coordinate-limit proof for the sequence space is written locally.

contents.name: 2.2 orthogonality and orthonormal systems
contents.result: The orthogonal-series facts used by the spectral multiplier are stated locally with the exact compact spectral theorem dependency.

contents.name: 2.3 the spectral theorem for compact operators
contents.result: The existing published compact self-adjoint spectral theorem supplies the orthogonal eigenspace decomposition; this pair does not recreate it.

contents.name: 4.1 regularization and parameter choice
contents.result: The regularization and parameter-choice analysis informs the local residual map; continuity, monotonicity and endpoint claims are proved in the carrier.

contents.name: 5.2 parameter choice and convergence rates
contents.result: The source-condition rate result is restated with the local penalty coefficient convention and proved for compact Hilbert-space operators.

contents.name: 6 tikhonov regularization
contents.result: The Tikhonov filter and qualification definitions are included with compact-operator conventions and local hypotheses.

contents.name: Corollary 6.1
contents.result: The local theorem proves the corresponding source-condition bias/noise rate and optimizes the parameter explicitly.

contents.name: Corollary 6.2
contents.result: The discrepancy discussion motivates the local exact-root theorem; the local claim is convergence under its stated range and noise assumptions.

contents.name: Theorem 6.5
contents.result: The regularized solution formula used by this pair is included in the spectral-filter definition; compact spectral properties are supplied by their declared theorem dependencies.

sources.title: Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 4: Regularization Methods
sources.locator: Complete 29-slide chapter fetched and inspected: slides 5–8 spectral filtering and TSVD; 11–18 discrete Tikhonov and singular filter factors; 22–23 perturbation; 25–29 monotone norms and L-curve. Hansen uses lambda_H squared in the penalty, converted locally by lambda=lambda_H^2.
sources.independent_treatment: Independent numerical treatment from Clason; this is Chapter 4 of the same Hansen slide series as Chapter 5 and is not counted as a separate independent treatment.

contents.name: Chapter 4: Regularization Methods
contents.result: The finite-dimensional Tikhonov filter motivates the local compact-operator filter; the infinite-dimensional definition and its dependencies are explicit.

contents.name: Matrix Problems
contents.result: The finite matrix least-squares and SVD setup is the context for the local smoother formula and leave-one-out derivation.

sources.title: Per Christian Hansen, Introduction to Inverse Problems, Chapter 5: Regularization Parameter Choice
sources.locator: Complete 27-slide chapter fetched and inspected: slides 4–6 bias/noise error split; 8 discrepancy principle; 10–14 L-curve; 15–18 leave-one-out, trace-average GCV and occasional failure; slide 23 summarizes heuristic limitations. Hansen uses lambda_H squared in the penalty.
sources.independent_treatment: Independent numerical treatment from Clason; the chapter is an additional part of Hansen’s full parameter-choice lecture material, not separately counted from his Chapter 4.

contents.name: More About the Forward Error
contents.result: The finite-dimensional bias/noise split motivates the local Hilbert-space result, whose spectral bias and noise terms are proved under explicit coupling.

contents.name: The Discrepancy Principle
contents.result: The finite bracketing and budget-exhaustion algorithm is included with exact endpoint and crossing conditions.

contents.name: The L-Curve for Tikhonov Regularization
contents.result: The source defines the continuous log-log curve; the local item deliberately specifies only a finite grid rule.

contents.name: The L-Curve Criterion
contents.result: A finite-grid maximum-curvature selection is included with its declared discrete Menger-curvature convention and tie rule.

contents.name: The Curvature of the L-Curve
contents.result: The local theorem verifies the finite-grid curvature values and least-index maximizer without asserting continuous optimality.

contents.name: The Prediction Error and (Ordinary) Cross-Validation
contents.result: The leave-one-out residual identity and its derivation are included locally for the finite linear smoother.

contents.name: Generalized Cross-Validation
contents.result: The finite score and tie-breaking grid rule are included; the exact minimizer property is proved locally.

contents.name: The GCV Function
contents.result: The finite GCV score differs by a fixed dimension factor from Hansen’s displayed denominator convention, which leaves its grid minimizer unchanged.

contents.name: Occasional Failure
contents.result: The one-observation example gives an exact finite case where the GCV tie rule selects the worse estimate.

sources.title: Gerald Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis, version November 17, 2017
sources.locator: Complete full-text PDF fetched; inspected the complete relevant passages in Chapter 1: sequence-space completeness, printed pp. 8–10, and the Hilbert-space example ell^2(N), printed pp. 17–18. Teschl refers to the analogous ell^1 completeness proof; this item supplies the complete ell^2 coordinate-limit proof locally.
sources.independent_treatment: Third independent treatment; used only for sequence-space and Hilbert-space context, not as a substitute for the local proof.

contents.name: §1.3 The geometry of Hilbert spaces
contents.result: This section supplies the Hilbert-space context; the local carrier proves the square-summable sequence space claim completely.

contents.name: §1.4 Completeness
contents.result: The full Cauchy-coordinate argument for completeness is included locally, beyond the source’s pointer to an analogous sequence-space proof.
